title: Sea-View Villa
summary: A G+1 contemporary villa with a timber-screened upper floor, framed to catch the sea breeze from Rushikonda hill.

story.challenge: A sloping 400 sq yd plot, salty coastal air and a family that wanted large glass openings without the heat that usually comes with them.
story.whatWeDid: We stepped the foundation with the slope, used M30 concrete with corrosion-inhibiting admixture for the coastal exposure, and shaded every west-facing window with a vertical teak-finish screen. The family received photo updates on WhatsApp every Saturday for 13 months.
story.result: Handed over 9 days ahead of schedule. The upper floor stays noticeably cooler in summer, and the final bill matched the signed estimate within 1.4%.

outcome: Handed over 9 days early · Final bill within 1.4% of estimate

review.text: The weekly photos meant we never had to chase anyone. We knew what was happening on site even from Hyderabad.

title: G+1 Family Home
summary: Two floors, two families. A ground-floor home for the parents and a first-floor home for their son, with separate entrances.

story.challenge: The family had a fixed budget and a firm move-in date before their daughter's wedding. Any delay or cost overrun was not an option.
story.whatWeDid: Fixed-price agreement before the first excavation, a full bar-bending schedule to cut steel waste, and a dedicated site engineer on site every working day. Cube tests on every slab pour were shared with the family.
story.result: Ready 3 weeks before the wedding. Zero change-order surprises: every extra the family asked for was priced in writing before it was built.

outcome: Moved in 3 weeks before the deadline · Zero surprise costs

review.text: Every extra was quoted in writing first. That alone made us trust them.

title: Heritage Home Renovation
summary: A 40-year-old family house that everyone said should be demolished. We kept its character and rebuilt everything that was failing.

story.challenge: Spalling plaster, rusted lintels, damp walls and a roof that leaked every monsoon, but the owners wanted to keep the house their grandfather built.
story.whatWeDid: Structural audit first, then jacketing of weak columns, full re-roofing with a waterproofing membrane, new wiring and plumbing, and a fresh facade that respects the original parapet details.
story.result: A home that looks and works like new, at roughly 55% of the cost of demolishing and rebuilding, with a 10-year structural warranty on the repaired frame.

outcome: Saved ~45% vs demolish-and-rebuild · No leaks through two monsoons

review.text: Everyone told us to knock it down. Ravi garu showed us the numbers and saved our grandfather's house.

title: Kitchen & Living Interiors
summary: A dark, cramped 1990s kitchen opened up into a bright modular kitchen that flows into a warm, timber-toned living room.

story.challenge: A closed kitchen with poor ventilation, no storage and a load-bearing wall in the way of the open plan the family wanted.
story.whatWeDid: Our structural engineer designed a steel beam to safely remove the wall. We fitted BWP marine-ply modular cabinets, quartz counters, a chimney with outside ducting and warm layered lighting.
story.result: Twice the counter space, a kitchen you can see the living room from, and a 9-week schedule that the family could live around.

outcome: 2× counter space · Finished in 9 weeks while the family lived in

review.text: They protected the rest of the house like it was their own. No dust anywhere after they left each day.

title: Retail & Office Block
summary: A G+3 retail and office building on the PM Palem main road, with a double-height glass showroom frontage.

story.challenge: A tight urban plot on a busy road, strict GVMC setbacks and an owner who had already signed tenants for the ground floor.
story.whatWeDid: We handled the plan approval paperwork, phased the work so the ground floor shell was ready first, and used a structural glazing system rated for coastal wind loads.
story.result: The ground-floor tenant moved in at month 12, four months before the building was complete, so the owner started earning rent early.

outcome: Ground floor rented out 4 months before completion

review.text: Phasing the work let our first tenant move in early. That paid a good part of the interest on the loan.

title: Leak-Proof Terrace & Bathroom
summary: Monsoon leaks were staining ceilings on two floors. We traced every source, sealed the terrace and rebuilt the worst bathroom.

story.challenge: Water was entering from a cracked terrace, failed bathroom tile joints and a hidden pipe joint, so earlier patch jobs never worked.
story.whatWeDid: Moisture-meter mapping to find every source, a polyurethane membrane on the 1,800 sq ft terrace with proper slope correction, and a full bathroom rebuild with a crystalline waterproofing coat under new tiles.
story.result: Dry ceilings through the next monsoon, and a written 7-year waterproofing warranty.

outcome: Dry through the next monsoon · 7-year written warranty

review.text: Three contractors patched it before. These people found the real cause in one visit.
